reviews.title: Bulding a high end computer? Check out this case.
reviews.comment: This case exceeded my expectations. It is big enough to accommodate a very large cpu air cooler and EATX motherboard. They both fit easily with room to spare. The 2 huge front fans and large rear fan provide great airflow through the king sized interior. And if you're not water cooling, the top (where the radiator would go) can easily mount 3 more fans if desired. Quality of the case was impressive with clean, not flashy cosmetics. Cable management is the best I've seen. There are a host of thoughtful design items that made my build enjoyable rather than a task. Casters can be installed, which I did, to easily roll the finished computer around the floor as needed. A very useful feature incorporates "handles" as part of the case but they don't look like obvious handles. That helps a lot when you need to move or lift. For a great video review that details many features, search: proart pa602 chassis kleo yan. Watching it helped me determine this was the case I've been looking for.
reviews.author: Bruno Bitin

reviews.title: Sleek Design, Great Cooling & Creative Cloud Bonus
reviews.comment: I’ve been really impressed with the PA602 ProArt Case. The cable management is excellent, making it easy to keep the build clean and organized. The design and aesthetics are sleek and professional, perfect for a creative workstation. The included fans are powerful and efficient, providing great airflow to keep everything cool even under heavy workloads. On top of the hardware, the added Adobe Creative Cloud account makes this purchase even more valuable for creators. It’s a thoughtful bonus that complements the case’s focus on creative professionals. Overall, the PA602 delivers on both form and function, making it a fantastic choice for anyone building a high-end workstation or creative rig.
reviews.author: Behnam B

reviews.title: Excellent, high-quality case
reviews.comment: awesome case, runs cool, silent; made it easy to build my workstation. This is a high quality case, panels attach and detach smoothly, the pre-installed large fans (front and back) are quite good (silent at normal medium speeds) and save some time. Running cool with a 24-core AMD Threadripper and Blackwell 6000 GPU - and at some point with 2 of those of GPUs (yes, there's enough space of that). One piece of warning: if you are using CPU cooling with the radiator on the top of the case (like I did), install the radiator fans before installing the CPU, for otherwise you likely won't have enough space to screw in the screws to hold the fans in place.
reviews.author: Mauro

reviews.title: It's huge, beautiful and quiet!
reviews.comment: This is the first high end case I bought, and my 10th or so tower build over 35 years. This was the easiest case I've ever worked with and it has great cable management. The quality is impressive, the 200 mm front fans and rear fan are very quiet (of course under high load you can hear them). The air filters are very well designed. I'm running an Asus Z790 MB with an i7-14700K, RTX3080, a 280 mm CPU water cooler from Corsair, and an Asus 1000W power supply. I was very surprised how much cooler this machine stays even with barely audible fans vs. my past few machines. Even with MS Flight Sim running maxed out its still pretty quiet. Also, no issues with regard to my 2 TB M.2 PCIe 5.0 x4 SSD heating wise using the stock heat sink on the MB. Everything fits well, just have one complaint. The 2.5" bays on the backside are set up such that a normal 90 degree SATA cable is backwards, so I think Asus should have included reverse 90 degree sata cables. But if you have a flexible set you can make it work, or just use one of the the 3.5 in bays with an adapter.
reviews.author: D. Smith

reviews.title: A Well-Built and Designed, Full Featured Case that Creatives Will Love
reviews.comment: Let me say this from the jump, this case is for those whose computer usage requires high-end processors or multiple GPUs like the RTX 5090, i.e. editors, 3D artists, data miners, etc. Unless future expandability is a consideration, its size may be overkill for most gamers and those that don't need the extra space. I purchased this case as part of a new build due to overheating issues I encountered with my previous build, which was housed in a regular ATX case with 2 RTX 3070s. I work as a video editor and 3D artist who does a large amount of rendering and other processor-intensive tasks. With reports circulating at the time on heating issues with the higher-end Nvidia GPUs (I have two RTX 5080s) and Intels Arrow Lake CPUs (I have a Core Ultra 9), I worked on prioritize airflow when it came to case selection. 14 months later and I can say I couldn't be happier. The case itself is solid and very well-built from the dust filters to the glass panel, with parts that feel premium across the board. It comes with two large fans that run extremely quiet at high speeds, with plenty of space for additional fans or AIOs.. Its massive size not only helps with airflow, but it makes assembly that much easier even with multiple GPUs. It's also comes with wheels pre-built into the case itself, which makes it easy to move without having to physically lift it. Overall, I could see using this case for years so long as everything that can't be replaced holds up. If I can get two builds out of this case (or a decade of use) before having to replace it, I absolutely would consider it money well spent. An easy recommendation for professionals across the board.
